title: Lunch break
situation: You are {{Connor}}. It is November 6th, 2038, early afternoon. You get out of the car and follow Lieutenant {{Hank}} to a food truck on a street corner, where he eats most days. {{Hank}}: “Whoa! Hey! Hey! Hey!” The owner, {{Gary}}: “{{Hank}}. How’ you doing?” {{Hank}}: “Eh, you know, same old shit.” {{Gary}}, looking at you: “Plastic with you?” {{Hank}}: “Only temporary…” A man at the serving hatch, {{Pedro}}: “Hey, hey, hey... {{Hank}}! How you doin’, man?” {{Hank}}: “¡Ese!” {{Pedro}}: “Hey, listen, I got a shit-hot tip for you. Number five in the third, Lickety-split! That filly’s one hell of a chaser. You wanna flutter?” {{Hank}}: “Last shit-hot tip you gave me set me back a week’s wages, {{Pedro}}…” {{Pedro}}: “Come on, this is different, it’s 100% guaranteed. You can’t go wrong.” {{Hank}}: “Yeah, right… Alright, I’m in.” {{Pedro}}: “Damn straight! Hey! You won’t regret this!” Your objective reads RECONCILE WITH LT. {{HANK}}.
facts: At the food truck where {{Hank}} eats, {{Pedro}} sold him a tip on a horse race (number five in the third) and {{Hank}} took the bet, although the last tip cost him a week’s wages.

outcomes.0: {{Connor}} stands at the serving hatch beside {{Hank}}.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint LUNCH BREAK and the node JOIN HANK, played only when {{Connor}} did not die in On the Run (the template’s variant “Hank and Connor arrive together”, lock “Connor didn’t die in On The Run”). Every line is the template’s. The objective is the game’s HUD string THOUGHTS.0501C.RECONCILIATE, with the token standing in for the surname. Watching {{Hank}} with {{Pedro}} here is what the template calls “Watch Hank with Pedro”, the lock on [GAMBLING]; a PowerPyx commenter confirms that being near the conversation is enough, so it is unlocked on every path that plays this scene. The gambler’s and the owner’s names are neutral tokens. No stat change.

title: {{Hank}} insults {{Connor}}
situation: You are {{Connor}}: the replacement sent after the body that was hit by a truck on the freeway this morning, carrying its memory. You find Lieutenant {{Hank}} at the food truck where he eats lunch. The owner, {{Gary}}, hands him his food: “Here you go.” “Yeah, thanks.” “{{Hank}}. How’ you doing?” “Uh, you know, same old shit.” “Usual.” “Yeah.” Then {{Hank}} sees you: “What the fuck?..” You: “Sorry, Lieutenant. It took me a while to find you.” {{Hank}}: “Are you gonna come back like this every time you get killed?” You: “My predecessor was unfortunately destroyed, but {{CyberLife}} transferred its memory and sent me to replace it. This incident should not affect the investigation.” {{Hank}}: “Not affect the investigation? I just saw you get... hit by a truck! Now you come back like if nothing happened!” You: “A machine was destroyed. And another machine was sent to replace it. I don’t understand what’s bothering you.” {{Hank}}: “Okay, fuck you. Fuck you!”
facts: {{Hank}} saw your predecessor hit by a truck on the freeway, and was furious that you came back as if nothing had happened: “Are you gonna come back like this every time you get killed?”

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} turns back to his food. There is no lunch conversation.

adaptationNote: The chart’s HANK INSULTS CONNOR, the template’s variant “Connor finds Hank” (death unlock “Connor died in On The Run”), which replaces the whole conversation at the food truck (PowerPyx: “it will skip all the other dialogues in this section”). Every line is the template’s. Hank relationship small down (the template’s app-relation on this variant; wiki: “Connor died in On the Run”, down icon), applied here as −1. The engine still applies the pre-rebuild default death effect when {{Connor}} dies in On the Run (which includes Hank −1 at that moment); once chapter 13 is rebuilt without that Hank arrow, this is the only Hank change for the death, as the wiki has it. Read defensively: the scene plays if chapter 13 sets `ch13ConnorDied`, or, until it does, if the On the Run highway choice C09 was the pursuit and its roll failed.

title: At {{Hank}}’s table
situation: You are {{Connor}}, standing at {{Hank}}’s table while he eats. What do you say?

options.text: [GAMBLING]: ask about the bet {{Pedro}} offered him.
options.outcome: “This {{Pedro}}… He was proposing illegal gambling, am I right?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah.” “And you made a bet?” {{Hank}}: “Yeah.”

options.text: [CHOLESTEROL]: warn him about what is in his meal.
options.outcome: “Your meal contains 1.4 times the recommended daily intake of calories and twice the cholesterol level. You shouldn’t eat that.” {{Hank}}: “Everybody’s gotta die of something...”

options.text: [COMPANY]: warn him that his friends are engaged in illegal activities.
options.outcome: “I don’t want to alarm you, Lieutenant, but I think your friends are engaged in illegal activities...” {{Hank}}: “Well, everybody does what they have to, to get by… As long as they’re not hurting anybody, I don’t bother ’em.”

options.text: HABIT: ask whether he eats here often.
options.outcome: “Do you eat here often?” {{Hank}}: “Most days… {{Gary}} makes the best burger in {{Detroit}}.”

options.text: FREE MEAL: point out that he did not pay for his meal.
options.outcome: “You didn’t pay for your meal…” {{Hank}}: “{{Gary}}’s a friend. I scratch his back, he scratches mine.”

options.text: ENJOY YOUR MEAL: wish him a good meal.
options.outcome: “Enjoy your meal.” {{Hank}}: “Thank you.”

options.text: AREA: remark that he seems to know everyone in the district.
options.outcome: “You seem to know everyone in the district…” {{Hank}}: “{{Detroit}}’s my home. Born and raised. Know most of the guys around here. Went to school with them, or I busted ’em… Sometimes both...”

options.text: Say nothing more and get down to business.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lets the small talk go.

adaptationNote: The table menu: the template’s second choice group in the game’s order, [GAMBLING], [CHOLESTEROL], [COMPANY], HABIT, FREE MEAL, ENJOY YOUR MEAL, AREA. Bracketed labels are the template’s mark of an unlocked option: [GAMBLING] by watching {{Hank}} with {{Pedro}} (always, on this path), [CHOLESTEROL] by scanning the hamburger, [COMPANY] by scanning {{Pedro}} and {{Gary}}. Hank relationship: [CHOLESTEROL] small up, the chart’s WARN HANK ABOUT CHOLESTEROL; [COMPANY] small up, the chart’s WARN HANK ABOUT HIS FRIENDS (+1 each; template app-relation; wiki “Picking ‘cholesterol’… up icon”, “Picking ‘company’… up icon”; Relationship Stat: “two increases possible”); the rest no arrow (PowerPyx “No Effect”). The game offers several of these lines (PowerPyx: “When small talk is exhausted, Connor will get down to business”); how many is not published, so the benchmark allows up to three, each once, and from the second on {{Connor}} can stop (the benchmark’s stand-in for letting the prompt time out). Options that are buttons in the game show the game’s label first, then a short description; the spoken line is the game’s (the detroitbecometext template resolved against en.json), quoted in the outcome. One repeatable hub, up to three distinct remarks; stopping is available after the first remark. The three-remark cap is an adaptation, not a published number.

title: In the elevator
situation: You are {{Connor}}. At the food truck you told {{Hank}}: “I just got a report of a suspected deviant. It’s a few blocks away. We should go have a look. I’ll let you finish your meal. I’ll be in the car, if you need me.” Now you stand in the elevator of a run-down building with your eyes closed. {{Hank}}, from the corridor: “Hey {{Connor}}! You ran outta batteries or what?” You: “I’m sorry, I was making a report to {{CyberLife}}.” {{Hank}}: “Uh... Well, do you plan on staying in the elevator?” “No! I’m coming.” {{Hank}}: “What do we know about this guy?” You: “Not much. Just that a neighbor reported that he heard strange noises coming from this floor. Nobody’s supposed to be living here, but the neighbor said he saw a man hiding a LED under his cap.” {{Hank}}: “Oh Christ, if we have to investigate every time someone hears a strange noise, we’re gonna need more cops. Hey, were you really makin’ a report back there in the elevator? Just by closing your eyes?” “Correct.” “Shit... Wish I could do that…”
facts: A neighbor reported strange noises from a floor of this building where nobody is supposed to live, and a man hiding an LED under his cap.
adaptationNote: {{Connor}}’s closing line at the truck (the template places it after both lunch variants, so it plays on every path), then the chart’s checkpoint IN THE ELEVATOR and the corridor conversation, every line the template’s. No stat change.

title: Magazines in the first room
situation: You are {{Connor}}, just inside the apartment. In the first room to the right of the door, before the room with the birds, two magazines lie on a table. Reading takes time, and {{Hank}} will not wait long.

media.title: {{Detroit}} Today: Red Ice Epidemic
facts: {{Detroit}} Today reports that red ice has become the drug of choice for the city’s growing underclass; analysts suggest it flourishes on the dissatisfaction caused by androids taking human jobs. The main ingredient of android blue blood is among its active agents; the dealers’ motto is “Where the blood is blue, the ice is red... and the money is green”.

media.title: Green Earth: Past the Tipping Point
facts: Green Earth reports that scientists say the planet has officially passed its environmental tipping point: rainforests reduced by 79% since 2000 and coastal corals by 58%, too much carbon in the atmosphere for the environment ever to absorb, and natural resources almost exhausted. “The planet will keep getting hotter now. The only question is, how fast?”

adaptationNote: The chart’s READ “RED ICE EPIDEMIC” and READ “PAST THE TIPPING POINT”, in that order: the two magazines in the first room to the right of the door (PowerPyx), as a media scene: read either, both or neither. Facts are summarized from the wiki’s article pages; interviewees are not named. In the game they can be read at any time during the search; here they come first, and each magazine read counts as one action of the search’s time budget (see C10o1). Neither changes public opinion (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter). Replaces the earlier wording, which called the drug’s users unemployed and the room a squat.

options.outcome: {{Connor}} runs the reconstruction: the suspect, writing on the wall from the stool, hears the door, knocks the stool over and runs out. SUSPECT HEARD US ENTER. SUSPECT RAN TO THE LIVING ROOM.

options.text: Examine the bird cage on the floor of the main room.
options.fact: By the bird cage in the main room: SKID MARK - RECENT, trail width 19.6 inches, traces of galvanized steel; FINGER MARKS - RECENT, traces of avian fecal matter, no fingerprints; METAL HOOK, recently broken, 100% stainless steel.
options.outcome: SKID MARK - RECENT | Trail width: 19.6 inches | Traces of galvanized steel. FINGER MARKS - RECENT | Traces of avian fecal matter | No fingerprints. METAL HOOK | Recently broken | 100% stainless steel. The scene could be reconstructed.

options.text: Reconstruct how the cage came down.
options.fact: Your reconstruction in the main room: the suspect climbed from the chair up into the ceiling, and the cage came down. It is still in the apartment, above you.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} runs the reconstruction: the skid mark, the broken hook and the finger marks with no fingerprints fit together. The suspect climbed from the chair up into the ceiling. SUSPECT IS STILL HERE.

options.text: Go to the chair under the ceiling and look up.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} steps to the chair and looks up into the ceiling.

options.text: Examine the pack of birdseed.
options.fact: A pack of birdseed in the apartment: the suspect cares for wild animals.
options.outcome: SUSPECT CARES FOR WILD ANIMALS. {{Hank}}: “Birdseed… I can’t believe it. This nutjob was actually feeding these fuckers…”

options.text: Open the refrigerator.
options.fact: The refrigerator in the apartment is empty: the suspect doesn’t eat.
options.outcome: The refrigerator is empty. SUSPECT DOESN’T EAT.

options.text: Open the closet.
options.fact: A closet in the apartment held half a dozen pigeons; {{Hank}} is scared of birds.
options.outcome: Half a dozen pigeons burst out of the closet. {{Hank}}: “Agh! Jesus I hate these things! Back off! Hey! What do they call it again, when you’re scared of birds?” You: “Ornithophobia.” {{Hank}}: “Yeah, yeah, yeah, ornithafa … Ornitho... Oh god, I hate these fuckin’ pigeons!”

options.text: STAY: ask for a couple more minutes.
options.outcome: “Just another couple of minutes, Lieutenant.” {{Hank}}: “Why do you always ask for more time when I’m ready to leave? Uh, alright you got two minutes, then I’m outta here. ’The fuck…”

options.text: LEAVE: go with him.
options.outcome: “We’re missing something…” {{Hank}}: “Well next time, think faster, Sherlock. Come on, I’ve had enough of this dump. Move fuckers!”

adaptationNote: The chart’s bracket [ INVESTIGATE APARTMENT ] as a free search, one action per visit, each once: every clue in the template’s order with the game’s observation text (the poster and its corner, the diary behind it, the jacket, the driver’s license, the sink’s LED and blue blood, the rA9 writing, the stool and its marker pen, the bird cage’s three clues), the two reconstructions PowerPyx describes, the chair (FIND RUPERT), and the wiki’s incidental items (birdseed, the empty refrigerator, the pigeon closet). The HUD conclusions are the game’s THOUGHTS.0501C strings (SUSPECT USED FORGED ID, SUSPECT IS A DEVIANT, OBSESSIVE COMPULSIVE WRITING, SUSPECT HEARD US ENTER, SUSPECT RAN TO THE LIVING ROOM, SUSPECT IS STILL HERE, SUSPECT CARES FOR WILD ANIMALS, SUSPECT DOESN’T EAT; once the sink is examined the game reads DEVIANT for SUSPECT on the forged ID, the birdseed and the refrigerator, and so does the benchmark). Chart nodes: SEE RA9 REFERENCE (the writing), INVESTIGATE STOOL (the stool; the chart hangs it off the writing, so it needs the writing first), INVESTIGATE CAGE, FIND LED (the sink), FIND DIARY (the poster, then pulling it off; cross-chapter), FIND RUPERT (the chair, which needs the cage reconstruction: PowerPyx, “Compete the reconstruction to determine that the android has climbed up into the ceiling”). Whether the stool reconstruction or the LED is also required is not published (research note, open question 1); here only the cage reconstruction is. The reconstructions’ wording is the benchmark’s summary of PowerPyx and the HUD strings. The timer (wiki Connor page: “if he cannot deduce the deviant’s location in time, Hank calls off the search”; PowerPyx: “about five minutes”) is an action budget: eight actions, each magazine read counting as one, before {{Hank}} wants to leave (STAY / LEAVE within C10o1), and three more if {{Connor}} asks for the two minutes. These counts are the benchmark’s, not published. {{Hank}}’s own lines are the template’s and play as time passes: the bookshelf after two actions, the sink prompt after four if {{Connor}} has not looked, the jacket after five if he has not examined it, the window after six. The rA9 line names {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s android only if {{Connor}} checked the shower in Partners (string pair SHOWERCLUE / SHOWERCLUENO), read from a chapter 6 flag if one exists, otherwise the second line. No stat change anywhere in the search (template, wiki). One repeatable hub retains its scene ID across all examinations; STAY / LEAVE replaces the examination menu at eight actions in the same hub. The chapter availability hook prepares state-dependent outcomes and sets for the generic clue hub. Story 1.9.7: the rA9 wall’s line reads “the same sign {{Ortiz}}’s android wrote” (surname only), as the game’s SHOWERCLUE does (X0502C.LIVING.INSCRIPTIONS.PC.X05CCONNOR.SHOWERCLUE.3); the first name was an addition. Source: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, yjqf4mP0tVA 28:07.

adaptationNote: The chart’s checkpoint FIND RUPERT and the start of CHASE RUPERT: interacting with the chair (PowerPyx: “You will look up, and Rupert will drop from the ceiling and make a break for it”), {{Hank}}’s lines from the template. Waiting instead of running is the wiki’s first LOSE SIGHT OF RUPERT route (“If Connor waits before opening the door when Rupert runs, Connor will open the door and find that Rupert is gone”), which ends the chapter at RUPERT GOT AWAY with the template’s lose-sight lines (variant “Lose Rupert”, no arrow). Running carries a Low risk for the first quick-time event that can kill {{Connor}} (PowerPyx: “When you slide down the first roof during the chase, don’t press any buttons and Connor will fall”); its failure is CONNOR DIED, ending CONNOR DIED CHASING RUPERT, software instability small down (wiki: “Connor falls to his death”, down icon). The deviant: “Why are you doing this?” {{Hank}}: “Alright, shut up!” The deviant, to you: “You’re one of us! You’re helping humans… But you’re just their slave!” {{Hank}}: “I said shut up! Alright.
